scenes.sub: Structure reserves so money is available when it's needed, earning a return at every tier.

scenes.vo: Here's the picture: The liquidity ladder.

scenes.title: Key ideas
scenes.vo: T0 Instant, Seconds, Stablecoins in the operating wallet, 1 month: $5,000. T1 Same day, Hours, Blue-chip stablecoin lending, split across 2 protocols, 5 months: $25,000. T2 Term, Scheduled, PTs maturing on dates you'll need the money (Lesson 10.1), Next 6–12 months of planned spending. T3 Growth, Days–weeks, Strategy positions, L.P.s, staking, The rest, within caps.
scenes.cap: T0 Instant, Seconds, Stablecoins in the operating wallet, 1 month: $5,000 T1 Same day, Hours, Blue-chip stablecoin lending, split across 2 protocols, 5 months: $25,000 T2 Term, Scheduled, PTs maturing on dates you'll need the money (Lesson 10.1), Next 6–12 months of planned spending T3 Growth, Days–weeks, Strategy positions, LPs, staking, The rest, within caps

scenes.sub: Banks match the timing of assets to the timing of what they owe. Your ladder: Refill downward on a schedule: T1 tops up T0 monthly; maturing PTs top up T1. Never fund a T0 need by selling a T3 position in a bad market. That's what the ladder exists to prevent.

scenes.sub: T0 $5,000 + T1 $25,000 = 6 months instantly available. T2 holds three PTs maturing in 3, 6 and 9 months, each sized for 3 months of spending. A −50% market day touches none of it.

lines: Why hold T0 in plain stablecoins earning little?
scenes.sub: Answer: Instant, certain access. It's the tier that pays today's bills without selling anything.
scenes.vo: Why hold T0 in plain stablecoins earning little? ... Pause and think. ... The answer: Instant, certain access. It's the tier that pays today's bills without selling anything.

scenes.sub: Answer: Known future spending, with maturities matched to when the money is needed and a fixed return locked in.

scenes.sub: Answer: Forced selling of growth positions at bad prices to meet short-term needs.
